title: Browser Web Chat continuity, retry, governance, and deletion
hard_gates: the root route serves a usable same-origin Web Chat application
a user can create and switch isolated conversation threads
a sent message reaches the conversation runtime and renders one assistant answer
refresh restores the selected thread and server-owned transcript
the operation identifier is persisted before the network request starts
retry after an uncertain response reuses the original operation identifier
replay renders no duplicate user or assistant turn
an offline send shows an explicit recoverable failure
an offline send creates no phantom assistant answer
network restoration allows the failed request to be retried
reviewable memory candidates are visible without exposing authority identifiers
a candidate can be accepted or rejected from the browser
current governed memory is visible for the selected thread
current memory can be corrected from the browser
current memory can be forgotten from the browser
forgotten memory is absent from a fresh turn and refreshed memory view
asynchronous send completion and failure update only the originating thread
an out-of-order inspection response cannot replace the active thread transcript or memory
desktop and mobile layouts keep the active composer visible without page-level overflow
same-origin assets use restrictive browser headers and the final clean reload has no console errors or warnings
non_claims: the deterministic browser run is not a real-model quality qualification
browser local storage is not memory authority
this case does not qualify a publicly exposed multi-user Web Chat deployment
